sections.h2: Choosing a sale route in Ocoee
sections.html:
A seller in Ocoee can go cash, list with an agent or sell without one. Repairs, deadlines and how much of the price you want in your pocket decide it. The city lies in Orange County, so you answer to the county's tax bill and to a city fire assessment printed on that same bill.

  • Cash sale: a good match for a leaking roof or a closing date that cannot move.
  • Agent listing: a good match when the house shows well and you can wait through showings and loan approval.
  • Sale by owner: fits a seller willing to draft the contract and arrange the deed personally.

Whichever route you take, have the year's unpaid tax and fire assessment settled in writing at closing.

Ocoee adds a yearly non-ad valorem fire assessment to property tax bills to pay for fire protection, and it is one of the amounts split between buyer and seller at closing. An ordinance adopted on August 6, 2013 authorizes it within city limits, and it shows up on the bill mailed each November.

Taxes follow property value, while a special assessment follows the benefit a property receives from the service. Residential parcels are measured by dwelling units and non-residential buildings by square footage. The city's equivalent dwelling unit is 2,423 square feet, the size it treats as the average house, and each residential dwelling unit counts as one unit.

How the Ocoee fire assessment works
DetailWhat the city sets
AuthorityOrdinance No. 2013-010, adopted August 6, 2013
BillingOn the property tax bill mailed in November

Equivalent dwelling unit size2,423 square feet

The city holds a public hearing each August at City Hall, 1 N Bluford Avenue, to set the final rate. Read the line item on the current bill rather than trusting last year's number. A notice about the assessment arrives by mail separately, and the city says it is not a bill.

sections.h2: Fire protection, insurance and property values
sections.html:
Ocoee ties the assessment to its fire protection classification with the Insurance Services Office, known as ISO, which it wants to preserve. Stronger fire service can support higher property values and lower insurance rates, while weaker service can push values down and premiums up. Special assessments can only pay for fire protection, unlike general taxes.

A buyer will look at the insurance quote right next to the asking price, so get your own homeowner's declarations page and be ready to share the premium and coverage. If you received a renewal notice recently, keep it with the rest of your papers. The city's notice was written to explain a proposed increase, so check the current bill for the amount that applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: Orange County tax dates around a closing
sections.html:
Your house is valued as of January 1 by the Orange County Property Appraiser, and the tax collector sends the bill in November. Your closing date therefore decides how the year's bill is shared with the buyer. The appraiser's website has a tax estimator for people planning to buy or sell, handy for previewing the next owner's bill before you set a price.

  • By March 1 you file for any exemption.
  • In August a proposed-tax notice comes in the mail, and you have 25 days from it to petition on value.
  • November brings the bills, with a discount for early payers that gets smaller every month through February.
  • April 1 is the delinquency date, and certificates are sold by June 1.

The homestead exemption can reach $50,000 in two layers. It ends when you sell, and the buyer files a new application.

sections.h2: Your capped assessment and the buyer
sections.html: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the assessment returns to just value and the buyer's opening bill can be far higher than yours. Buying another Florida home? Portability may let you carry part of your cap along, as long as the new homestead is established within three years of the January 1 of the year you left the old one. The portability form goes in with the exemption application, so talk to the property appraiser before you sign the next contract.

The City of Ocoee takes development and building applications through its website, where building applications sit under Apply and development projects and annual budgets sit under Find. To see what construction is planned near your listing, begin with the development projects page. A buyer's agent will probably look there too.

Inspections tend to uncover unpermitted work. A porch, garage conversion or addition built without a permit is worth a call to the city's building staff before you list, to learn what it would take to close it out.

Foreclosure in Florida is a court process, and the auction follows final judgment. It takes place 20 to 35 days later, unless the plaintiff agrees to wait, and the high bidder puts down 5 percent. Bids above the debt produce surplus money, and homestead owners should ask the clerk about it within 10 days of the sale.

Selling before the auction lets you pay the lender from the proceeds and pick your own closing date.

sections.h2: Stamp tax on an Ocoee deed
sections.html: Each deed carries stamp tax of $0.70 per $100 of consideration, and every signer is answerable for it. The Orange County clerk of courts collects the payment when the deed is recorded. Page-based recording fees and smaller per-name and technology charges come from section 28.24, and the settlement statement totals them.

sections.h2: Steps once you accept an offer
sections.html: Expect the title company to hunt for liens and unpaid taxes, so collect payoff letters, your latest tax bill with the fire assessment line and any permit paperwork. The closing agent can explain how the fire assessment and property tax are split, and you can confirm it on the settlement statement. Cash buyers skip the appraisal and loan approval, the stages where financed deals often slow down. At signing you execute the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. If anyone on the title lives out of town, raise remote signing options early.

faqs.q: Is the Ocoee fire assessment a tax?
faqs.a: It is a special assessment, and the city separates it from property tax. Taxes follow property value, while the assessment follows the benefit a property receives from fire protection. It still appears on the same November bill.

faqs.q: Who covers the fire assessment at an Ocoee closing?
faqs.a: The contract and the closing statement settle that. Most sales prorate the year's bill between seller and buyer, so look for the assessment line on your settlement statement and ask the closing agent how it was divided.

faqs.q: Where do I take questions about an Ocoee assessment notice?
faqs.a: Phone the City Clerk's Office at (407) 905-3105. The letter the city mails about the assessment is neither a bill nor a fine.

faqs.q: Does my Ocoee homestead exemption survive the sale?
faqs.a: No. The exemption follows your permanent residence and is lost once the home stops being that residence. File a new application on your next home by March 1.

faqs.q: Do I owe Florida estate tax on an inherited Ocoee house?
faqs.a: No. Florida's estate tax ended for deaths after December 31, 2004, and since July 1, 2023 personal representatives no longer file the old state forms. Probate steps and creditor deadlines still apply, so ask a probate attorney.
